original_question: Assume that a classical integrable system (p1 , . . . , pn ) is given on M . Does there exist a quantum integrable system (P1 , . . . , Pn ) such that pj = σ(Pj )?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1, Problem 6.1 in the PDF version inspected (renumbered as Problem 7.1 in the later ar5iv/v2 HTML): the general quantization-existence problem for a given classical integrable system.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation and matches Problem 6.1 almost verbatim: it asks whether a given classical integrable system (p1, ..., pn) on M admits a quantum integrable system (P1, ..., Pn) whose principal symbols satisfy pj = σ(Pj).
missing_details: The ambient classical phase space M is a symplectic manifold of dimension 2n.

The tuple (p1, ..., pn) should be understood as a classical Liouville integrable system: smooth real-valued functions on M with {pi, pj} = 0 for all i, j and with dp1, ..., dpn linearly independent almost everywhere.
"Quantum integrable system" in the paper does not mean arbitrary operators: it means n semiclassical operators on a quantum Hilbert space corresponding to M.
The operators P1, ..., Pn are required to be self-adjoint: Pj* = Pj.
They must commute exactly, [Pi, Pj] = 0 for all i, j, not merely modulo O(h^∞).

The symbol map σ is the principal symbol in a semiclassical quantization framework where principal symbols are defined; the paper specifically mentions pseudodifferential operators and Berezin-Toeplitz operators as the main examples.
The paper’s definition of independence on the quantum side is encoded at the symbol level: the principal symbols pj = σ(Pj) must have almost everywhere independent differentials.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should state that the equality σ(Pj) = pj is required for every j = 1, ..., n.
refined_question: Let (M2n, ω) be a symplectic manifold, and let p = (p1, ..., pn) be a classical Liouville integrable system on M, meaning that the pj are smooth real-valued functions with {pi, pj} = 0 for all i, j and with dp1, ..., dpn linearly independent almost everywhere on M. In a semiclassical quantization of M for which a principal symbol map σ is defined, does there exist a quantum integrable system P = (P1, ..., Pn) on the corresponding quantum Hilbert space—namely, n semiclassical self-adjoint operators with exact commutation relations [Pi, Pj] = 0 for all i, j—such that σ(Pj) = pj for every j = 1, ..., n?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s exact official problem, not a neighboring one: Problem 6.1 asks precisely whether a given classical integrable system (p1, ..., pn) on M admits a quantum integrable system (P1, ..., Pn) with prescribed principal symbols pj = σ(Pj). To make the question stand alone and paper-faithful, one must import the nearby definitions supplied in Section 6.1: a quantum integrable system consists of n semiclassical self-adjoint operators that commute exactly and are independent in the sense that their principal symbols have almost everywhere independent differentials. The introduction supplies the underlying Liouville-integrability assumptions for the classical tuple. I did not replace this with the polynomial-in-momenta questions from Section 6.3, because the paper explicitly presents those only as more specific versions of this general problem.
